guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / panic attack and grounding
title: Hyperventilation triggered by blood sight
setting: Camping festival. 26F soldier with history of PTSD has hyperventilated and panicked at the sight of her friend's open hand bleed.
verdictExplanation: Anxiety/PTSD episode triggered by blood sight, severe hyperventilation, and altered mental status. Sick: manage, reassure, and monitor.

shared.danger: Blood from friend's hand (being treated by colleague)

history.history: Saw friend's hand cut open, triggered a severe panic attack 5 minutes ago

followUp.question: What is the appropriate first aid management for this hyperventilating patient?

options.text: Move her away from the sight of blood, sit her down, encourage slow controlled breathing, and reassure her
Force her to breathe into a paper bag to stop hyperventilation
Call 999 for an emergency ambulance immediately
Slap her face to snap her out of the panic attack

followUp.explanation: Move the patient away from the trigger (blood sight). Sit her down, encourage slow, controlled breathing, and provide calm reassurance. Paper bags are dangerous. 999 is not indicated for a simple resolved panic attack.

evolvingStage.narrative: Despite your initial reassurance, the patient's hyperventilation continues to worsen. She becomes increasingly dizzy, complains of tingling in her fingers, and suddenly faints.

followUp.question: The patient has fainted and is currently unresponsive, but breathing normally. What is your immediate priority?

options.text: Place her in the recovery position, monitor her breathing, and check for any injuries from the fall
Immediately start CPR as she is unresponsive
Sit her upright and splash cold water on her face to wake her up
Administer an auto-injector in case it is a severe allergic reaction

followUp.explanation: For an unresponsive patient who is breathing normally, the priority is airway protection using the recovery position. CPR is not indicated, and forcing an unresponsive patient upright is dangerous.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Move away from blood, sit down. Reassure and guide breathing.
levelFlags.erNotes: Ground the patient, check BGL, monitor SpO₂ and BP. Provide high-flow oxygen only if indicated (though usually hyperventilation has SpO₂ 99-100%).
